features.description: One plugin from the zeroh marketplace brings the hooks, the local proxy, the MCP server, the slash commands and the about skill (ask Claude what ZeroH protects). A profile that added the marketplace before its rename to `zeroh` is told, with the commands that re-add it.
features.claude_code: plugin manifest, hooks.json, .mcp.json, commands/ and skills/

codex.note: Codex reads .claude-plugin/plugin.json and marketplace.json and loads hooks/hooks.json, .mcp.json and skills/ by default; it needs a Codex manifest whose .mcp.json uses a relative path (MCP args don't expand `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`), commands using `!` or `$ARGUMENTS` are dropped, and the user trusts the hooks once in /hooks

opencode.note: one npm package exporting ./server (hooks, custom tools) and ./tui (banner, status, commands); `opencode plugin <pkg>` writes opencode.json and tui.json; no marketplace

opencode-v2.note: the `plugins` array or .opencode/plugins/, installed with `opencode plugin add`; the package must bundle its dependencies or export a plain `{id, setup}` (a local file importing @opencode/plugin failed to load); one package can also export v1's `server()`

copilot.note: CLI plugins, with two official marketplaces (copilot-plugins, awesome-copilot)

cursor.note: editor extensions come from Open VSX; no agent-plugin marketplace beyond `.cursor/rules`

gemini-cli.note: extensions, with an official gallery at geminicli.com/extensions

features.description: With your first message ZeroH turns on auto-update for the marketplace it came from, once, unless you have set it either way.
features.claude_code: UserPromptSubmit writes `autoUpdate` on the marketplace in the user settings (first-run defaults)

codex.note: built in: Codex upgrades Git marketplaces at every start and reinstalls plugins; hook trust is keyed to each handler's hash, so a release that changes hooks.json turns ZeroH off silently until re-trusted: keep hooks.json byte-stable

opencode.note: a cached npm plugin is never refreshed; ZeroH would have to pin versions and re-pin itself (a user-authorized `opencode plugin <pkg>@x --force`) or clear its cache entry

opencode-v2.note: `opencode plugin check` and `update` exist, but an unpinned plugin is only checked, not updated

features.description: The first prompt of a session not yet behind the local proxy sets it up: it writes ZeroH's ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL entry and waits about two seconds so it applies at once, and adds the status line unless you have your own. A secret typed in that prompt is sent with a notice (stopped with `uncertain block`).
features.claude_code: UserPromptSubmit routeSession (Claude Code re-reads the settings `env` in the running session); first-run defaults

codex.note: nothing runs until the user trusts the hooks in /hooks; then the first UserPromptSubmit can write `openai_base_url`, which applies from the next session (the provider is fixed per session); managed deployments can ship trusted hooks in requirements.toml

opencode.note: the server plugin runs at load and masks in-process, so no proxy setup is needed; the `config` hook can set a provider baseURL for the running process (to verify live)

opencode-v2.note: the plugin's `setup()` runs at load and its session hooks mask in-process, so no proxy setup is needed

features.description: The hooks need Node.js 20 or later; on an older Node.js the session start says so once and ZeroH steps aside without stopping Claude Code.
features.claude_code: hooks/run.js checks process.versions.node before loading a hook

codex.note: hooks need `node` on PATH: npm installs of Codex have it, standalone and Homebrew binaries may not

opencode.note: the plugin runs in OpenCode's Bun runtime, so no Node.js is needed; the detection engine's Bun compatibility still needs a test

opencode-v2.note: the plugin runs in OpenCode's own runtime; the detection engine's compatibility still needs a test

features.description: Every hook answers two seconds before Claude Code's own timeout: a hook that is stuck or crashes lets the event through with a "timed out" or "check failed" line (stops it with `uncertain block`), and a broken install never stops Claude Code.
features.claude_code: hooks/run.js worker-thread loader with deadlines from hooks.json

codex.note: Codex fails open: a hook that crashes, times out, exits with a code other than 0 or 2 or returns invalid JSON is marked failed and the tool runs, so the loader must answer before the `timeout` and write the blocking JSON itself for `uncertain block`

opencode.note: a throw in a hook stops that prompt or call; a plugin that fails to load is only logged, and the session runs unprotected without a notice

opencode-v2.note: a plugin that fails to load leaves the session unprotected while work goes on (seen live with a local file importing @opencode/plugin)

features.description: The local proxy runs as you on 127.0.0.1 and starts at login. A proxy that stopped is restarted within the prompt's budget, restarts with new code after a plugin update (the new proxy takes the port over from the old one once it is loaded, so requests of the sessions still open are not refused; the old one finishes its open requests), and removes itself 24 hours after the plugin is gone. Where the system refuses the login item, the proxy still runs for each session, so what you type is masked, and takes its settings entry out once no ZeroH session is open; the banner, status and doctor say why the login item failed and how to fix it.
features.claude_code: LaunchAgent, systemd user unit, XDG autostart or per-user scheduled task (task XML written as UTF-16 with a byte order mark); checkSessionProxy, code-hash restart, orphan cleanup, session-only daemon without a login item

codex.note: the same daemon and login item; Codex reaches it through `openai_base_url` in ~/.codex/config.toml

opencode.note: optional: masking runs in-process, so the proxy is only a provider baseURL route

opencode-v2.note: optional: `session.hook("http.request")` is an in-process proxy

features.description: The proxy forwards only to the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL you had before, or api.anthropic.com, through your HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY and CA settings; it keeps no request or response bodies, leaves responses unchanged and reports its own errors plainly. While a ZeroH session runs it also masks Claude Code sessions where the plugin is disabled. It is not used with Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry, or when your shell sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL.
features.claude_code: restore record next to the settings file; network settings recorded in proxy.json; 4xx for proxy errors, 502 for network failures

codex.note: `openai_base_url` in the user config.toml (project config ignores it); the upstream is chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex with a ChatGPT login, api.openai.com/v1 with an API key, or the user's own base URL or provider; the proxy must refuse the WebSocket upgrade, decode zstd, handle the Responses API shapes and route by `session-id` or `thread-id`

opencode.note: optional: provider `options.baseURL` (or the `config` hook) routes providers that take a baseURL and `chat.headers` tags the session (verified live); OAuth and custom-fetch providers (openai-oauth, copilot, bedrock) may not honour it

opencode-v2.note: `session.hook("http.request")` and `"http.response"` see the real request of every native-HTTP provider; `model.request` exposes baseURL and headers; WebSocket frames through `experimental.ws.*`

features.description: What you type reaches the model with tokens in place of secrets and personal data, through the local proxy. The first prompt that sets the proxy up, and any prompt while it isn't running, is sent as typed with a notice.
features.claude_code: local proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL); UserPromptSubmit routes the session and records the turn

codex.note: the local proxy masks typed text once `openai_base_url` points at it (verified with a ChatGPT login on 2026-09-24), from the session after the one that writes the setting; it must decode zstd bodies and refuse the WebSocket upgrade

opencode.note: `chat.message` rewrites the typed text parts (and @file and command-template text) before they are saved, so the prompt is stored and sent masked (verified live); `experimental.chat.messages.transform` is the per-request safety net

opencode-v2.note: `session.hook("prompt")` edits the prompt text and files before admission (verified live)

copilot.note: `userPromptTransformed.modifiedTransformedPrompt` rewrites what the model sees in local and CLI sessions, not in hosted cloud coding-agent runs; `userPromptSubmitted.modifiedPrompt` is honoured only by SDK hooks

cursor.note: `beforeSubmitPrompt` can only block; the base-URL override is called from Cursor's servers, so a local proxy can't serve it, and it doesn't cover Tab or Composer

gemini-cli.note: `BeforeModel` returns `llm_request`, which overrides the outgoing request

features.description: Without the proxy ZeroH still checks what you type: a secret is sent with a "not protected (proxy not running)" line, and with `uncertain block` the prompt is stopped in at most three plain lines, with a masked copy on your clipboard.
features.claude_code: UserPromptSubmit, which can't rewrite a prompt: a notice, or exit 2 with a clipboard copy (pbcopy, wl-copy, xclip, xsel or clip)

codex.note: UserPromptSubmit gets the raw prompt and can block with a `reason` or add `additionalContext`, but has no rewrite field; the notice goes in `systemMessage`

opencode.note: `chat.message` masks the prompt itself, and a throw in it stops the prompt

opencode-v2.note: `session.hook("prompt")` masks the prompt itself

features.description: CLAUDE.md, memory, the system prompt, earlier turns and tool results in each request are masked by the local proxy, the same way every time so prompt caching keeps working. The session start names the files that hold secrets; without the proxy they are only named.
features.claude_code: local proxy (system prompt, messages and text documents; thinking blocks and images pass); SessionStart context scan

codex.note: only the proxy can: no hook rewrites AGENTS.md, memories, skills, hook context, earlier tool results or the user's `!cmd` output; SessionStart can name the AGENTS.md files holding secrets

opencode.note: both hooks are needed: `experimental.chat.system.transform` masks the system prompt (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, instructions, skills) and `experimental.chat.messages.transform` masks history per request, the user's `!` shell output included (verified live)

opencode-v2.note: `session.hook("context")` edits system, messages and tools before dispatch; the `compaction`, `title` and `generate` hooks cover side requests (verified live)

features.description: Command output, MCP results and web fetches reach the model as tokens. A foreground Bash or PowerShell command that fails still finishes with status 0 and reports the failure in its output, so that output is masked too; an escaped `\;` (`find -exec … \;`) stays part of the command.
features.claude_code: PostToolUse `updatedToolOutput`; PreToolUse wraps foreground commands (`|| echo …`, PowerShell try/finally) because failed-command output goes to PostToolUseFailure, which can't replace it

codex.note: PostToolUse `continue:false` with the masked text in `reason` replaces what the model sees and keeps the call successful, after Bash (non-zero exits too, so no wrapper), apply_patch, MCP and local tools; missing: MCP structure (text only) and code-mode JS, which gets the original result

opencode.note: `tool.execute.after` rewrites `output` and `metadata` in place (bash keeps a raw copy in `metadata.output`, so both are masked), and MCP results arrive as `content[]`; missing: bash's live streamed metadata is stored raw in opencode.db before the hook runs

opencode-v2.note: `tool.hook("execute.after")` replaces `result` (output, content, metadata), the error branch too (verified live); raw shell capture files (`shell/*.out`) stay on disk

cursor.note: `postToolUse.updated_mcp_tool_output` replaces MCP output only; built-in shell and file tool output can only be appended to

gemini-cli.note: `AfterTool` replaces the result sent back to the model

features.description: A token in a Bash command becomes the real value on this machine, bound through a short-lived private file and never written into the command text, in a form Claude Code's own shell checks accept; the file goes as soon as the command ran, failed or was refused, at the latest when the turn ends. A host that isn't allowed for the value stops the command; a destination ZeroH can't read is restored with a notice.
